full_judgment:
13. Mr Fazlul Haq khan Farid, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the convict-appellant submits that there is no eye witness of the occurrence and as such the prosecution has hopelessly failed to prove its case. He further adds that non examination of vital witnesses raises a presumption to the effect that had been examined, they would not have supported the prosecution case and benefit of such defect will go to the convict-appellant. He further adds that since as per version of the PW 14 there assembled a third stranger person at the time of occurrence, the convict-appellant has no obligation to explain as to how the deceased met his death. 

 68. We find that all the other four eye witnesses made 164 statements before the Magistrate but none of them have come forward to depose before the Court. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the convict-appellant vehemently argued that non examination of those vital Witness particularly the inmates of the house raises a presumption as per section 114(g) of the Evidence Act against the prosecution to the effect that had they been examined they would not be have supported the prosecution case and benefit of those defect will go to the convict-appellant. Before giving to the benefit to the convict- appellant we find that all those eye witnesses were close relative of the convict-appellant and they still-remained in the custody of the convict- appellant and hostile witness Khaleda Pervin from where those four witnesses refrained from coming before the court to depose." Thus we find no justification to afford any benefit to the defence in the attending fact and circumstances of the case. Rather it can be 'safely said that the convict so to say the PW 14 resisted them from appearing before the court with an apprehension that the cat 'would be out of the bag. One of the makers of the 164 statement namely Mofizuddin was being adduced as defence witness No. 1 with plea to support the 3rd case of the PW 14. But this DW 1 is not also an eye witness of the occurrence. He also deposed that on hearing the sound of opening fire he rushed to the spot and saw the dead body of the deceased. In his 164 statement he clearly stated that after his arrival on the spot all the inmates reported to him that it is the convict appellant who opened fire towards the deceased whereupon he succumbed to his injury instantly, He instead of, deposing on behalf of the prosecution, he was examined in this case as DW 1 with a view to create contradiction and anomaly in the prosecution case. Thus we are not in position to place reliance upon him. However he deposed with view to support the PW 14, to the effect that there was an unknown person who came with the deceased who might have opened the fire: But the PW 4 Zamal uddin is a ballistic expert who categorically deposed that the fire as has been opened toward the victim was opened from the shotgun of the convict-appellant. There is no scope to hold that it was the third personwho could open fire 'towards the deceased from his gun. PW 14, Khaleda Pervin Baby is a hostile witness. The evidence of hostile witness can be taken in to consideration to' that extent which is consistent with the fact and; attending circumstances of the case. The PW 14 has been suggested that during the: course of giving 164 statements before the Magistrate, she admitted his guilt of her husband (convict-appellant) to the effect that none but her husband opened the fire which directly hit to the deceased. The 164 statement of a witness can no way be used as substantive piece of evidence. It can only be used in cross-examination of the witness in order to show that the evidence give in the court was false. To our estimation the PW 14 is a dubious witness who instead of speaking the truth, has tried to save the convict- appellant. Thus we are of the opinion that her statement can easily be discarded to that extent which is not consistent with-the circumstances of the case.
